result.title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep
result.summary: The ability to learn and generalize from limited experience, or sample efficiency, is a cornerstone of intelligence. How can we build language models that turn a few user interactions, a few snippets of unfamiliar code, or a handful of experimental results provided in context into knowledge that generalizes? Prior work has found that sleep, a process where the model performs $N$ recurrent forward passes to refine its representations of a chunk of context, can improve long-context reasoning (specifically, within SSM-attention hybrid models). We study whether this method also improves in-context adaptation on general, non-synthetic tasks for transformer language models. To this end, we pre-train language models up to 1.2B-parameters on up to 100B tokens with sleep mechanisms. Notably, longer sleep (i.e., using a larger number of recurrent forward passes $N$) enables the model to learn faster in-context on multiple few-shot algorithmic, question-answering tasks, while also achieving lower next-token prediction loss on out-of-distribution evaluations. On held-out code, models with $N=2$ and $N=4$ match the no-sleep baseline's loss using $2.10\times$ and $2.39\times$ fewer tokens in-context, respectively. More broadly, we view our work as a step toward building models that have better tradeoffs between in-context adaptation and decoding latency.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在最多 1.2B 参数、100B token 预训练的 transformer 语言模型中加入「sleep」机制，即对一段上下文做 N 次循环前向以精炼表示，并考察其对少样本上下文适应和分布外损失的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 不涉及视觉，但其固定次数循环前向更新上下文表示的做法，可能为 LVR 的 latent 状态迭代、动态计算及「适应收益—解码延迟」权衡提供方法线索，N 是否可自适应可供核查。
